title: Floquet Reservoir Engineering for Remote Logical Entanglement
abstract: Implementing controlled dissipative dynamics is a powerful approach for state preparation in a variety of contexts, including the preparation of remote entangled states. Here, we show that by going beyond the standard setting of time-independent dissipative dynamics, one can realize even more powerful non-unitary protocols. We introduce dissipative Floquet protocols for stabilizing remote entanglement of logical qubits, where continuously-running dissipation is interleaved with a periodic sequence of unitary gates. These protocols harness existing experimental capabilities, and overcome time-entanglement limits that constrain standard approaches. They also implement an autonomous form of entanglement distillation. We show how these protocols give enhanced protection against waveguide loss, and as an example, analyze a specific implementation using cat-qubits and transmons in a superconducting circuit.
summary: The paper introduces dissipative Floquet protocols to stabilize remote logical entanglement between qubits. By interleaving controlled unitaries with continuous engineered dissipation, the system autonomously performs entanglement distillation, achieving high fidelity even in the presence of waveguide loss. This offers a powerful pathway for quantum networking that bypasses the need for explicit measurements.
main_problem: The goal is to deterministically stabilize remote logical entanglement between qubits using non-unitary, dissipative protocols that mimic measurement-plus-feedback without requiring explicit classical communication.
main_result: The proposed Floquet reservoir engineering protocol autonomously acts as an entanglement distillation engine, achieving steady-state stabilization of the Bell state and demonstrating error scaling proportional to waveguide loss ($\propto \epsilon$).
method: The method involves interleaving continuous engineered dissipation (Lindblad dynamics) with periodic fast unitary gates within a Floquet cycle ($E = E_{ZZ} \circ E_{XX}$) to drive the system toward an entangled steady state.
model_or_system: The physical realization uses two remote nodes, each containing logical qubits protected by encoding schemes like cat or GKP states. The coupling is mediated by a dissipative reservoir (waveguide) described by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Steady-state concurrence ($C$), entanglement fidelity, and the scaling of the steady-state error ($1-C$) with loss ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\gamma$), time scales ($	au_{stb}, 	au_{conv}$), waveguide loss parameter ($\epsilon$), and squeezing/squeezing parameters ($r$ or $\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the ability to implement fast, controlled unitary gates (e.g., CZ) and relies on analyzing the system dynamics via perturbation theory in the weak-loss limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup showing two remote nodes coupled by an engineered dissipative bath; one figure shows the stabilization rate vs. loss $\epsilon$, and another plots logical steady-state entanglement $C$ versus squeezing parameter $r$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of dissipative Floquet protocols, details the EZZ subroutine for parity encoding/transduction, analyzes the convergence rate via correlator evolution equations, and concludes with error scaling analysis under weak loss ($\epsilon$).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally relevant framework for quantum networking by showing how dissipation itself can be engineered to perform complex tasks like entanglement distillation, bypassing limitations of standard unitary protocols.

Floquet reservoir engineering to stabilize re- mote logical Bell states (a) Two remote computational nodes (A and B) each consist of a logical qubit (depicted as a surface code patch) and a communication qubit (repre- sented by a transmon). The communication qubits are cou- pled via an engineered entangling dissipative bath Lent. (b) Circuit description of one period of the protocol: entangling engineered dissipation acts continuously on the communica- tion qubits, interspersed with fast controlled unitary gates. The gates partition the dissipation into finite-time channels M(τ) ≡exp(τLent).

FIG. 3. Optimal steady-state concurrence error 1 −C versus waveguide loss ϵ for communication-qubit-only stabilization via Lent (blue circles), and the full logical Floquet protocol (orange squares). The two panels are for the TMS and Rabi schemes, with (τstb, τconv) optimized at each ϵ. Both Flo- quet protocols exhibit linear scaling in the small-loss regime whereas communication-qubit-only stabilization scales sub- linearly ∼ϵ1/2. Below ϵ ∼10−2 the logical protocol out- performs the Lent-only protocol.

FIG. 4. Stabilization of remote cat-qubit Bell state. Pulse sequence (top) and circuit diagram (bottom) for one stabilization cycle, using the Rabi-driven entangling reservoir Lent [Eq. (10)]. Within a cycle, Lent is activated on the trans- mons for two time intervals (τstb, τconv), interleaved with dis- persive CNOT gates of duration tg and single-photon-driven cat phase gates S; the two-photon cat stabilization Lcat acts continuously to protect the logical states.

FIG. 6. Typical protocol run time Texp as a function of the communication-qubit entanglement. The non- monotonic dependence yields a clear optimum, set by the tradeoff between larger conversion rate pconv and slower sta- bilization τent as the entanglement increases.
